title: Grilled Sardines in Spiced Roasted Tomato Sauce
author: Zoe Adjei
desc: The sauce ingredients roast twenty-five minutes before the sardines join them — and the kenkey is boiled eight to ten minutes until fork-tender.
longDesc: Twelve whole fresh sardines in a roasted tomato sauce, served with a ball of Ga kenkey sliced into eight discs. The sauce is built by roasting rather than frying: half a red onion, four large quartered tomatoes, ginger, garlic, black pepper, curry powder, extra-hot chilli powder, chilli flakes, stock, tomato purée and salt go into a 180-degree oven for twenty-five minutes. Then the sardines go in for fifteen to twenty minutes until cooked through. Meanwhile the kenkey is boiled eight to ten minutes until fork-tender and sliced. It is the only documented recipe that cooks with kenkey rather than just serving it alongside.
ingredients: 12 whole fresh sardines, scaled, gutted and washed
2.5 cm piece fresh root ginger, grated
steps: Put the onion, tomatoes, ginger, garlic, black pepper, curry powder, chilli powder, chilli flakes, stock, tomato purée and salt into a roasting dish.
Add the sardines, the lemon juice and a drizzle of olive oil.
Cook 15 to 20 minutes, until the sardines are cooked through.
Meanwhile boil the ball of Ga kenkey 8 to 10 minutes, until fork-tender.
Serve the sardines and sauce with the kenkey discs.
chefTips: Roast the sauce for twenty-five minutes BEFORE the fish goes in. Roasting rather than frying the tomato gives a sweeter, deeper sauce and it is why this works.
Fork-tender at eight to ten minutes is the kenkey cue, and this is the only documented recipe that gives one for cooking a ready-made kenkey ball.
Slicing the kenkey into eight discs rather than serving a lump is a plating choice and a good one — it soaks up the sauce.
Fifteen to twenty minutes for whole sardines in a hot sauce. They are small and oily and they go from done to dry quickly.
Lemon juice goes in WITH the fish, not at the end. It cooks into the sauce.
Half a teaspoon each of curry powder, extra-hot chilli powder and chilli flakes is a restrained hand for this cook. The roasting does more of the work than the spicing.
Ga kenkey is bought here, not made. If you want to make it, that is GHA037 and it takes three days.
commonMistakes: Adding the sardines at the start.
Serving the kenkey as a lump.
Frying the sauce instead of roasting it.
Boiling the kenkey past fork-tender, so it disintegrates.
sources: Adapted from 'Grilled Sardines in a Spiced Roasted Tomato Sauce' by Zoe Adjonyoh, published on stylist.co.uk, 5 February 2021. BYLINE AS PRINTED: 'By Stylist Team'; the page intro credits the recipes to Adjonyoh. Quantities confirmed across two fetches (TWO-PASS). Yield as printed: 'Serves: 4'.

Ingredients exactly as printed: ½ red onion, sliced; 4 large ripe tomatoes, quartered; 2.5cm piece fresh root ginger, grated; 1 garlic clove, chopped; ½ tsp coarsely ground black pepper; ½ tsp curry powder; ½ tsp extra-hot chilli powder; ½ tsp dried chilli flakes; 100ml vegetable or chicken stock — one fetch added 'good-quality'; ½ tbsp tomato purée; ½ tsp sea salt, plus extra; 12 whole fresh sardines, scaled, gutted and washed; 1 tbsp fresh lemon juice; olive oil, for drizzling; ball of Ga kenkey, to serve.

Method as printed: oven 180°C / Gas Mark 4; roast the sauce ingredients 25 minutes; add the sardines and cook '15–20 minutes until sardines cooked through'; boil the kenkey and 'cook 8–10 minutes until fork-tender', then slice into 8 discs.

THE KENKEY CUE, 'fork-tender' at 8-10 minutes, is the ONLY documented instruction in this collection for cooking a ready-made kenkey ball. Every other kenkey entry covers making it from scratch. That makes this a genuinely useful cross-reference.
A TITLE INCONSISTENCY worth noting: the recipe is called GRILLED sardines but the method ROASTS them in the sauce in an oven. The method is followed above.
FERMENTATION: Ga kenkey is a bought ingredient here and is boiled, not prepared. Its own three-day fermentation is documented at GHA037.

This is one of three recipes published together on the same Stylist page; the others are the jollof fried chicken (GHA102) and the spinach and agushi curry (GHA105), with the jollof dry spice mix (GHA101) and a chalé sauce printing also on it.
storage: 2 days refrigerated. Oily fish does not keep well.
reheating: Gentle oven heat. Do not stir, or the sardines break up.
healthBenefits: Sardines are among the richest sources of omega-3 fats, vitamin D and calcium, eaten whole with their bones.
Roasted tomato is high in bioavailable lycopene.
Very low in mercury compared with larger fish.
Kenkey's fermentation improves the meal's mineral absorption.
culturalNote: Kenkey with fried fish is the Accra street meal, and this takes the same pairing and roasts it into a single dish — sardines in a spiced tomato sauce with kenkey discs to mop it up. Sardines are also the most sustainable fish in the recipe book and the cheapest, which is worth saying.
